title: Source-grounded evidence audit of the 2,5-CT interstellar-sulfur claims in OTA-SCI-0026
question: Audit the exact declared OTA-SCI-0026 source text against the primary publication Araki et al., 'A detection of sulfur-bearing cyclic hydrocarbons in space', Nature Astronomy 10, 401-409 (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41550-025-02749-7, and the current interstellar-sulfur literature. Which [R]-marked claims are directly supported (first interstellar detection of 2,5-cyclohexadiene-1-thione / C6H6S, 13 atoms, largest sulfur-bearing molecule in the ISM, cloud G+0.693-0.027 at ~27,000 ly, 92 rotational lines, laboratory synthesis plus IRAM 30m / Yebes 40m validation, MPE Garching under Dr. Mitsunori Araki) and which are misstated, unverified or superseded (e.g. thiophenol already detected in meteorites, the claimed up-to-1000x interstellar sulfur depletion factor, the exact publication vs. press-release dating of 26 January 2026, 'molecular resonators' framing)? Do not reconstruct the document from neighboring files.
why_now: The underlying Nature Astronomy paper is real and very recent (online late 2025, issue January 2026); the document was archived on the press-release date and asserts several specific empirical details — especially the meteoritic-thiophenol precursor claim, which the paper's abstract does not obviously establish — that only primary-source verification can confirm or correct. Confirming the [R] layer now fixes a canonical science document while the source literature is still current.
real_world_anchor: Araki et al., Nature Astronomy 10, 401-409 (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41550-025-02749-7 — first interstellar detection of 2,5-cyclohexadiene-1-thione (C6H6S) in Galactic-centre cloud G+0.693-0.027.
novelty_reason: Prior topics audited OTA-SCI-0037 (RHIC/STAR spin correlation) and OTA-FND-0030 (chi-field/Hexade boundaries) plus the mtDNA/biophoton and Bronze-Age/copper anchors; none touch interstellar sulfur astrochemistry or this Nature Astronomy detection. Distinct document, distinct real-science claim, materially new.
